quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle requires:

options.text: You to swerve to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction to be safe. Do not swerve suddenly on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: During the day, your headlight should:

options.text: Switch between high and low beam.

questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day. This helps other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: The right footwear for riding a motorcycle should have:
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels may catch on surfaces. Tuck in laces so they don't catch on anything.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. To stay safe, a rider should:

options.text: Sound the horn repeatedly at night.
Stay in front of other vehicles so their headlights see you.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night: slow down, increase your distance from other vehicles, use the headlights of cars ahead to see farther, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), and be flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: As the motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can use more front brake pressure.
Should use less front brake pressure.
Can use more rear brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can use more front brake pressure.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward during braking, the front wheel has more traction. This means you can apply the front brake harder.

questions.question: When loading cargo on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, the safest way is to:
questions.explanation: The safest way is to go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to approach at a right angle can be dangerous because you may enter another lane.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane gives three paths of travel for motorcyclists: left, center, and right.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit and other regulatory signs are usually rectangular. They are white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This discourages the other driver from re-entering your lane too soon.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors and you are not familiar with them, you should practice because:

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. But they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Get used to your convex mirrors before riding.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Remain in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve as separate actions, not at the same time. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.question: _______ guarantees that another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.

questions.question: When loading a motorcycle:

options.text: Place heavier items toward the front.
Place heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place loads forward with heavier items in the front. Loads should be over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: In a group ride, less experienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This keeps them from having to chase the group. More experienced riders can also watch them from behind.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Accelerate while keeping the brake on.

questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if the rear wheel locks on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you fully stop.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while going through a curve?

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle leans, the tires use some grip for turning. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: If you must brake while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more slowly than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you leave the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more slowly than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, the tires have less grip than when it is upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, press the brakes smoothly and slowly.

questions.question: A small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve into another lane to avoid the animal.
Change lanes as fast as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.explanation: Avoid hitting an animal if you can do so safely. However, when riding in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane to miss a small animal could cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is less dangerous than hitting another car.

questions.question: A driver is following you too closely. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the driver.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the driver.
questions.explanation: If a driver is tailgating you, flash your brake light before slowing down. The tailgating driver may be focused on you and not see road hazards ahead that require traffic to slow.

questions.question: How does motorcycle stopping distance compare to car stopping distance?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, stopping distance is about the same for motorcycles and cars. However, wet or slippery roads make it harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.
